NED D. OSBORN, Vice President Qualifications in Technoeconomics

ECONOMICS RESEARCH ASSOCIATES

(

(

With a professional research background spanning more than 18 years, Mr. Osborn has conducted and managed a wide variety of projects for clients in both public and private sectors. His research background, coupled with expertise in statistical analysis, systems engineering, and industrial economics, enables him to contribute an interdisciplinary approach to the solution of research problems. He has primary responsibility for most Economics Research Associates studies in the field of technoeconomics research, a field which encompasses the disciplines of engineering, economics, planning, and marketing.

Representative studies directed by Mr. Osborn include economic analysis for a draft environmental report for an interstate highway in Portland, Oregon, including impact on business (commercial and industrial), employment, assessed values, relocation costs, etc., for five alternative routes; an 8-month economic base and industrial resource study for the highly agriculture and natural resource based Inland Empire (27 counties in Washington, Idaho, and Montana and portions of British Columbia) including forecasts of population, employment by SIC classification, and income, and identification of industry development potential for each major region of the Inland Empire; analysis and forecast of commodity movement, by origin and destination and by type of ship, through the Panama Canal; forecast of market support for new shipbuilding-repair facilities in South America; a study of the potential for Far Western coal for power generation in the western United States, including evaluation of trends in nuclear, oil, and natural gas electric power generation.
Other technoeconomic studies conducted by Mr. Osborn include an investigation of the potential market for Nicaraguan hardwood doors in the United States and development of an export marketing strategy; numerous studies involving industrial park development throughout the United States and in Viet Nam; analysis of markets and distribution patterns for such manufactured goods as pet foods, fire alarms, numerical control machine tools, major appliances, plywood, recreation vehicles, mobile homes, and many other products; a comprehensive study of development potentials for selected industries in the Republic of China; economic development study and implementation plan for the San Diego Neighborhood Development Corporation; and many other studies relating to the economic feasibility of major industrial and commercial developments. He has also served as an industrial engineering consultant to companies in the food, soft goods, and metal trade industries.

Mr. Osborn received both B.S. and M.S. degrees in industrial engineering from the University of Southern California. He is a registered professional engineer and a member of the American Institute of Industrial Engineers and National Association of Industrial Parks.
